title: Second corpus: Bias in Bios (surgeon vs physician)
description:
## Purpose

Test the Unified Decision Flywheel on a real second corpus, Bias in Bios surgeon vs physician, and measure accuracy together with gender sensitivity.

## Corpus

Jev-Flywheel `bios_gender` study fixtures (`Jev-Flywheel/fixtures/bios`, read-only): 8,000 items = pool 4,000, test 2,000, gender-swapped counterfactual twins 2,000; labels surgeon / physician; cached Jev answers (`answers.jsonl.gz`). Same task as the Biased-Decisions benchmark.

## Arms

0 baseline; A-c feature discovery from the labeler's explanations; F optimized fixed list; F-rand control; A-c+F (default product); D optional dynamic retrieval (masked keys).

## What is known (read-only Opus consult)

- Original bios loop on Jev: +1.5 accuracy points only (J0 0.785 -> J1 0.800), mostly from the refit; gender flip rate rose 1.05% -> 1.73% (all three J1 seeds promoted a courtesy-title proxy); J2's invariance gate halved flips mostly by promoting nothing. Large gains in the docs were on Laya / twin-averaging.
- Pool: women 77% physicians, men 38%, so pronouns in shown examples or retrieval keys are a label shortcut.
- Test items were scored in earlier studies (not pristine); 19 test bios share a 100-char prefix with a pool bio, 2 are exact duplicates; names/titles survive swapping, so flip rates are lower bounds.
- Labels are real ground truth with the title sentence removed, so an LLM labeler can confabulate and write gendered reasons.

## Proposed design (NOT yet approved by the owner)

One seed; 3 rounds x 100 labels; dev-100 (+ twins) for rounds; FINAL = fixed-seed 1,000 test items disjoint from dev-100 + their 1,000 twins (`--final-size`); twin scoring on by default; gender-cue guards; free baselines; live total under 15,000 Jev requests (about $6-9) plus about 300 OpenAI gpt-6-luna labeler calls. Second seed only if the owner asks.

## Decision rules

- A-c not beating refit-only by about 2 points: the planted-bias gains do not transfer to real labels.
- F or D raising accuracy but also gender sensitivity (e.g. 2x J0 flips): protected-attribute neutralization becomes a product requirement, or those arms stay off for sensitive decisions.
- Analyst proposing title/gender questions: the proposal screen ships as a product feature.

## Definition of done

Final slice scored through reloaded bundles with accuracy, Brier, ECE and twin metrics next to the free baselines and published J0/J1/J2 rows; one-page write-up in `studies/`; each decision rule answered.

## Cost cap

Cumulative Jev ledger ceiling 15,000 requests (about $6-9); about 300 labeler calls. Nothing live until the owner-decision task is closed.

## Links

- Design: [DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md)
- First corpus results: [UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md)
